title: Observable Geometry for Effective Quantum Circuits
authors: Huan-Hsin Tseng, Hsin-Yi Lin, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Yan Mong Chan, Tzu-Chieh Wei, Shinjae Yoo
abstract: We study redundancy and effectiveness of Variational Quantum Circuits via algebraic and geometric views of Lie groups. Considering unitary transformations acting on Hermitian observables, a stabilizer group decomposition is given. Subsequently, we identify the Hermitian orbit with a quotient space of a symmetric space. Through this connection, we characterize the effective circuit degrees of freedom. Our approach of spectral decompositions and homogeneous spaces yields tractable calculation criteria, which are verified by numerical experiments.
summary: This work develops a geometric framework using Lie group theory to analyze the redundancy inherent in Variational Quantum Circuits. By mapping the search space onto a homogeneous manifold defined by the stabilizer group of the Hamiltonian, it provides an explicit formula for the effective degrees of freedom. This theoretical insight is validated through numerical experiments on VQE optimization.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the redundancy and effectiveness of Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) by characterizing the geometry of the space of achievable effective Hamiltonians.
main_result: The dimension of this effective Hamiltonian manifold is determined by the structure of a stabilizer group $S$, yielding $\dim(	ext{MH}) = \dim(U(V)) - \dim(S)$.
method: The authors use Lie group theory, identifying the space as a homogeneous quotient space ($S\setminus U(V)$), and employ spectral decompositions to derive tractable dimension formulas.
model_or_system: The model involves VQAs (like VQE) acting on an $n$-qubit system defined by a Hamiltonian $H$. The circuit search space is mapped onto the orbit space $	ext{MH}$ under unitary transformations.
key_observables: Effective Hamiltonians ($	ext{MH}$), Stabilizer Group ($S$), and the Overlap Score $s(A)$ used to diagnose generator redundancy.
important_parameters: The dimension of the system ($n$) and the structure/eigenspaces of the Hamiltonian $H$ (determining $\dim(S)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on treating the problem using the mathematical framework of Lie groups and homogeneous spaces.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometric setup showing how unitary evolution maps observables, identifying the redundant component $S$. Figure 2 shows the distribution of overlap scores $s(A)$ for tested circuit generators.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical connection between observable redundancy and quotient spaces using Lie theory. It then derives dimension formulas based on the stabilizer group structure. Finally, it applies these concepts to a numerical VQE experiment, testing generator candidates using the overlap score $s(A)$.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (homogeneous space geometry) to quantify how much information is truly encoded in variational quantum circuits, which is crucial for designing efficient algorithms.
